findings.title: Unscoped deleteMany hard-deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` or `scheduled: false` filter. It hard-deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount above 1, whatever its channel (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) and whether it is already scheduled. Only the SMS path writes retryCount today, so the immediate impact is small, but the predicate is broader than the feature described and will silently delete rows for any future channel that uses the counter. There is also an edge case: if Twilio accepts a message but the follow-up update to scheduled:true throws, the row stays scheduled:false, its retryCount can reach 2, and it gets deleted while the Twilio message is still pending. Cancellation via referenceId can then no longer find it. The clause should be scoped to `method: SMS, scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Transient provider errors permanently drop reminders after two attempts
findings.body: Every failure consumes the retry budget equally: a falsy return from twilio.scheduleSMS (lines 178-186) and any exception (lines 189-199). The code does not distinguish permanent errors (e.g. invalid phone number) from transient ones (Twilio outage, rate limiting, network timeout). Two failures in consecutive cron runs cause the deleteMany at line 38 to remove the reminder permanently. The deletion is not logged and the user is not told. A brief provider blip is enough to lose reminders for every booking in the window. Consider backing off, counting only permanent error types, or at least logging each deletion.

findings.title: Unguarded update inside catch can abort the whole batch
findings.body: The catch block now performs a prisma.workflowReminder.update (retryCount) with no try/catch. If that update throws, the exception escapes the for-loop, so the remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped and the handler rejects. One concrete trigger: a reminder deleted between the findMany and this point (for example by a booking cancellation or a concurrent cron run) makes Prisma throw P2025, and that is not handled. A transient DB error has the same effect. Before this PR the catch block only logged, so this is a new failure mode. Guard the update, or make per-reminder error handling non-throwing.

findings.title: retryCount incremented from a stale read instead of atomically
findings.body: The new value is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at line 48, not read from the database at write time. If two cron invocations overlap, or the row changes between read and write, increments are lost (both read 0 and both write 1), so the retry limit can be exceeded. The same pattern appears at line 184. Prisma's `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` performs the increment atomically in the database.

findings.title: Empty message or missing recipient is never counted as a failed attempt
findings.body: The retry increments only happen inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. When the message resolves to empty, or the recipient is null (an SMS_NUMBER step with no sendTo, or a booking with no smsReminderNumber), nothing is scheduled and retryCount is not incremented. Such a reminder is re-attempted on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That unbounded retry is the behaviour this PR is meant to stop, so these cases should count as failures too.

findings.title: Comment no longer describes what the deleteMany does
findings.body: The comment says it deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed. The query now also deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or date, and it deletes unscheduled rows too. The comment is misleading for anyone maintaining the cleanup logic. It should describe both conditions.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes deletion semantics and adds retry bookkeeping in three places (the failed-schedule branch, the catch block, and the deleteMany), but adds no tests. Coverage should include: a failed schedule increments retryCount; a reminder with retryCount 2 is deleted on the next run; a successful schedule does not increment retryCount; and the deletion is scoped correctly. Without tests, the off-by-one around `gt: 1` and the scoping problems above are easy to get wrong.

findings.title: Generated Prisma-derived artifacts may not be regenerated
findings.body: Adding a column to WorkflowReminder changes what the generators in this schema emit (the kysely generator writes to ../kysely/types.ts and the zod generator writes to ./zod). The PR touches only schema.prisma and the migration. If those generated files are committed in this repository, they are now stale: typed queries will lack retryCount, and any drift check in CI will fail. Confirm whether the generated outputs need to be regenerated and included.
